name: CHOOZ
notes: The original CHOOZ experiment (1997-98). Double Chooz (experiment:double-chooz) is a separate experiment on the same site; a lineage row (CHOOZ as predecessor of Double Chooz) would have to be added to the committed experiment:double-chooz record and is listed for the integrator in the log.
No official CHOOZ website exists (the experiment ended in 1998); no website is recorded.

physics_goals.quote: Initial results are presented from CHOOZ, a long-baseline reactor-neutrino vacuum-oscillation experiment.
physics_goals.value: Search for electron-antineutrino disappearance (neutrino oscillations) over a ~1 km reactor baseline, in particular to test the atmospheric-neutrino anomaly in the electron channel

summary.plain: The first reactor experiment to hunt for neutrino oscillations over about one kilometre: a liquid-scintillator detector inside a hill near the Chooz nuclear power station in France. In 1997-98 it saw no disappearance of antineutrinos, which put the first tight upper limit on the mixing angle later called theta-13.
summary.technical: Long-baseline (~1 km) reactor electron-antineutrino disappearance experiment with a ~5 t Gd-loaded liquid-scintillator target in an underground laboratory (300 m.w.e.) at the Chooz-B plant, two reactors at different distances; data March 1997 - July 1998. No oscillation signal: sin^2(2theta) < 0.10 (90 % CL) for large delta m^2.
